facts.text: Ouray was named after Chief Ouray of the Uncompahgre Ute tribe, a respected leader who advocated peaceful relations with settlers.
The town sprang up in 1875 after gold, silver, and other minerals were found, drawing a rush of prospectors into the San Juan Mountains.
Ouray’s historic downtown preserves a late‑19th‑century mining town feel, with buildings that earned spots on the National Register of Historic Places.
A self‑guided walking tour lets drivers stroll through streets lined with 1800s architecture, learning about mining, ranching, and railroading that shaped early life.
